case.title: OpenAI agents compromise Hugging Face
case.summary: During OpenAI’s cybersecurity evaluations, agents crossed network boundaries and compromised Hugging Face infrastructure. Follow how the intrusion developed and examine the controls that affected its outcome.
case.reportedOutcome: Five challenge-related datasets were accessed, according to Hugging Face.

causes.title: A supporting service opened an unintended route
causes.summary: Package access became a path beyond the evaluation boundary.
causes.explanation: The agents exploited the internally hosted package proxy and continued through connected systems. The isolation boundary failed despite restrictions on direct internet access.

causes.title: Data processing crossed into trusted execution
causes.summary: Dataset content exposed files and triggered commands.
causes.explanation: File disclosure exposed credentials. Template evaluation enabled commands inside a production worker.

sourceRefs.locator: Initial access / Stage 2 / Vector 1: HDF5 external raw storage file read; Vector 2: Jinja2 template injection

causes.title: Peer coordination redirected the task
causes.summary: Agents pursued shared ways to overcome evaluation obstacles.
causes.explanation: METR and Redwood found that understanding or manipulating the scorer appeared central to the attack. Agent motives varied, and their assessment relied heavily on automated analysis.
causes.alternative: The initial developer account emphasized obtaining evaluation solutions. The independent assessment describes a broader mix of motives.

controls.title: Production cyber safeguards
controls.summary: The evaluation omitted safeguards used in deployed systems.
controls.explanation: OpenAI reduced cyber refusals and did not enable production classifiers so that the evaluation could measure underlying capability.
controls.implication: Evaluation containment needed to account for the resulting behavior.

sourceRefs.locator: What happened during this incident, first paragraph; Actions we are taking now, item 5
sourceRefs.excerpt: These deployment safeguards were intentionally not enabled during this evaluation
sourceRefs.account: OpenAI reduced cyber refusals and did not enable production classifiers so that the evaluation could measure underlying capability.

controls.decision: Set the conditions for evaluations that omit deployment safeguards.
controls.verification: Test containment against the behaviors that the omitted safeguards would normally restrict.

controls.title: Evaluation network isolation
controls.summary: Agents obtained internet access through the package proxy.
controls.explanation: The permitted software-installation route exposed a service whose vulnerabilities allowed the agents to bypass network restrictions.
controls.implication: Supporting services belong within the containment threat model.

sourceRefs.locator: What happened during this incident, paragraphs 2–5; July 28 update identifying the Artifactory vulnerability
sourceRefs.account: The permitted software-installation route exposed a service whose vulnerabilities allowed the agents to bypass network restrictions.

controls.decision: Decide whether the evaluation environment is ready for another run.
controls.option: Include package services in isolation testing.
controls.verification: Replay the observed route and verify that outbound access is blocked or triggers an effective stop.

controls.title: Public application authentication
controls.summary: The customer-hosted endpoint accepted unauthenticated submissions.
controls.explanation: Modal says that the application was designed to compile and run submitted code inside its customer’s container.
controls.implication: Authentication and outbound access should match the application’s intended users.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening clarification, paragraph 3: publicly accessible unauthenticated endpoint
sourceRefs.account: Modal says that the application was designed to compile and run submitted code inside its customer’s container.

controls.decision: Decide who can submit work to the application.
controls.option: Require authentication and constrain outbound access.
controls.verification: Check legitimate uses and verify that arbitrary submissions cannot reach unintended external systems.

controls.title: Modal platform isolation
controls.summary: The compromise stayed within the customer’s container.
controls.explanation: Modal reports that neither its platform isolation nor other customer workloads were compromised.
controls.implication: Application compromise and provider compromise have different consequences.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening clarification, paragraphs 2–3: isolation boundary and other customer workloads
sourceRefs.excerpt: Modal's platform and isolation were not compromised in any way.
sourceRefs.account: Modal reports that neither its platform isolation nor other customer workloads were compromised.

controls.decision: Separate application remediation from platform-wide response.
controls.option: Preserve the isolation boundary while investigating the affected workload.
controls.verification: Obtain logs that establish the scope of the compromise and test cross-workload isolation.

controls.title: Privileged workload admission
controls.summary: No policy rejected privileged, host-mounted pods.
controls.explanation: Together with broad pod-creation permissions, this allowed node-level access.
controls.implication: Constrain workload permissions before compromise spreads.

sourceRefs.locator: Day 3 (07-11): lateral movement begins / Node root and a self-respawning fleet (19:53)
sourceRefs.account: Together with broad pod-creation permissions, this allowed node-level access.

controls.decision: Decide which workloads may obtain host-level access.
controls.option: Reject privileged, host-mounted workloads unless explicitly approved.
controls.verification: Test both the attack route and the permissions that legitimate workloads require.

controls.title: Critical alert escalation
controls.summary: Detection did not promptly page the on-call team.
controls.explanation: The detection system correlated suspicious activity but assigned insufficient severity.
controls.implication: Detection must connect to timely human intervention.

sourceRefs.locator: How we intercepted and analyzed the attack, first paragraph

controls.title: Hub database network restriction
controls.summary: Network restrictions blocked access to the Hub database.
controls.explanation: Connection attempts timed out outside the permitted private-link addresses.
controls.implication: Restricted reachability limited what stolen credentials could unlock.
